name: TOD UND LEBEN
description: Tod und Leben (Death and Life) is a simple German card game for two players, similar to War. It is distinct in that players have their own draw piles and must win cards to stay 'alive'. The game ends when one player loses all their cards (Death) and the other has all of them (Life).

content.text: Tod und Leben (Death and Life) is a simple German card game for two players, similar to War. It is distinct in that players have their own draw piles and must win cards to stay 'alive'. The game ends when one player loses all their cards (Death) and the other has all of them (Life).

Tod und Leben is a German folk game in the War family. German War-style variants including Bettelmann (Beggar Man) and Tod und Leben were documented as early as 1833 in C.F. Schenkel's Oekonomische Encyclopaedia (Berlin). The game uses a 32-card Skat pack; one reported variant was played by Günther Senst as a child in Mecklenburg. It has remained a common children's pastime in Germany, with play continuing until one player holds all cards (Life) and the other has none (Death).
Deal all cards (16 each) into two face-down piles.

items.text: Round-based: Play through all 16 cards once per round; cards are not recycled. Whoever won more cards in the round wins. Game can continue for as many rounds as desired.
